text: Aspiration [Lat. ad + spirare , to breathe upon]: Ger. Aspiration ; Fr. aspiration ; Ital. aspirazione . In the system of Christian ethics, aspiration is an integral element in the theory of the genesis of Christian character. Faith in the Gospel possesses, as one of its most important consequences, a power of generating aspiration, i.e. either a 'longing desire' for reconciliation with Christ, or an 'overmastering determination' to lead the Christian life so far as possible. Literature : DORNER, Christ. Eth. (Eng. trans.), 363 f. ( R.M.W .)
